items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The code is mostly clear and `.window()` has JSDoc. However, `windows.map((w) => { const inner = ...` uses a single-letter name. The ternary `inner.queryChunks.length > 0 ? ...as (${inner}) : ...as ()` produces the same output either way, so it reads as confusing redundancy.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The spec builder is shared, but the window-name validation in `.window()` is pasted five times instead of using a shared assert. The WINDOW-clause mapping block is also repeated in every dialect. `window.ts` lives in `sql/expressions` rather than the `sql/functions` location the conventions ask for.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Inputs are checked at every boundary: `ntile`/`nthValue` reject non-positive integers, `preceding`/`following` reject negative, NaN, Infinity and fractional values, the frame `from <= to` order is enforced, and empty or whitespace-only window names throw. Numeric arguments are emitted inline, never as bound params. No errors are swallowed.

items.name: Public API additions are additive and consistent across dialects
items.name_zh: 公共 API 新增保持向后兼容且各方言一致
items.evidence: The change is purely additive. Each of the five `*SelectConfig` types gets an optional `windows?: { name; spec }[]` field, and an identical `.window(name, spec): this` is added to the pg, mysql, sqlite, gel and singlestore builders. `windowSql` is undefined when no windows are set, so existing SQL is unchanged. No existing exports were altered.
